title: Email: Fw: Metaphors in your Ausmus's Fault article

content.subject: Fw: Metaphors in your Ausmus's Fault article

content.text:
Anthony Fenech
Tigers beat writer
Detroit Free Press
(734) 752-9667
Twitter: @anthonyfenech
From: Tom Neely <timbuktom1@gmail.com>
Sent: Friday, September 11, 2015 11:05 AM
To: Fenech, Anthony <afenech@freepress.com>
Subject: Metaphors in your Ausmus's Fault article 
 
Hello Anthony,   You know you are my favorite sports writer. Your pieces dominate the Freep's Tigers coverage today. Good! I took a look at the metaphors in one of the pieces:

You used seventeen separate metaphors in the "Ausmus's Fault" article. And you switched metaphors twenty-two times. (The metaphor of the ship surfaces six times.) Is this too much? Of course we readers do understand what you wrote, and it is impossible to write without any metaphors. But, seventeen/twenty-two, in a short piece? This may be something to think about.
Cheers! Tom Neely, Grand Rapids, 616-826-1539, timbuktom1@gmail.com
